- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, model tends to under-forecast sharp upward moves; adjust upward by 2–5% for early spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and forecast is rising, model often over-optimistically extrapolates; cap upward trend at 1–3% above recent peak.
- After a strong upward spike (true > 85), model frequently over-estimates continuation; apply downward correction of 3–8% in next 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 80+ → 70–75), model often holds too high; reduce forecast by 5–10% for 3–5 days post-reversion.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0) and history shows volatility, model tends to smooth out noise; increase forecast volatility by ±2–3% to match true range.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 1–3% buffer to end of forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
